inclusion_rule: Brain-signal (ECoG, sEEG, intracortical, EEG, MEG) speech or language decoders whose ledger text names a speech unit and decoding or classification; the design of interest is the use-time prior over outputs: language model, grammar or finite-state network, pronunciation lexicon, or a context prior derived from another decoded utterance (for example a decoded question constraining the answer). A study counts under every design its full text names (upper bound); priors used only in training do not count; versions once.

read_fulltext.quote: Combining these Gaussian ECoG phone models with language information in the form of a dictionary and an n-gram language model , the Viterbi algorithm calculates the most likely word sequence and corresponding phone sequence .

In future work, we plan to expand the HMM-based classification scheme into a real-time continuous speech decoder that uses language modeling and Viterbi decoding (similar to a real-time version of the system described in [ 10 ]).
The system implements a Viterbi decoder that incorporates phoneme likelihood estimates from a linear discriminant analysis model and transition probabilities from an n -gram phonemic language model.
On the second day, the size of the possible output vocabulary increased to 125,000 words, and, after 1.4 additional hours of training data, the neuroprosthesis achieved 90.2% accuracy.
